source.basis: Operator spec page; structured facts only, no operator prose reproduced.

reading.body:
Ohio's eight disclosing data centers publish 60.4 MW of IT capacity, and CyrusOne's CIN2 near Cincinnati accounts for 11 MW of it, about 18 percent.

The more useful number is the gap. Ohio has 77 mapped data center facilities, and only eight publish an IT capacity figure. The state's 60.4 MW total is therefore a floor assembled from the minority of operators willing to state a number, not a measurement of Ohio's actual compute footprint. For AI specifically, that matters because siting decisions turn on where power exists, and a market where roughly nine in ten mapped facilities disclose nothing cannot be assessed for available headroom.

CIN2 itself is a mid-sized facility. Its 11 MW spans 143,778 square feet of technical space, which at the 40 kW per rack density used here as an assumption works out to roughly 275 racks, a configuration estimate rather than a published specification. Its certifications, PCI DSS, HIPAA, ISO 27001, FISMA, and SSAE 16 Type II, point toward regulated enterprise and government workloads rather than frontier model training. It ranks third among the eight Ohio facilities that publish capacity.

What the data does not cover is as important. There is no announced expansion, no grid interconnection detail, no power supply contract, and no utilization figure. The suitability score of 57 is derived only from published IT capacity and operator type. Nothing here shows whether Ohio's grid constrains AI scaling, only that no such constraint has surfaced in the facility disclosures that exist.

suitability.basis: weighted mean of the published inputs named here, scaled to 100; formula on the methodology page
